minutes.headline: Committee kept grade 9 school choice closed and set multi-year preschool tuition increases; superintendent retiring.
minutes.summary: The chair announced the superintendent's retirement at the end of the school year. The committee voted on school choice, closing grade 9 but allowing current students in grades 10-12 to stay under choice, and debated preschool tuition and a possible added part-time preschool teacher and classroom space. It also held a first reading of a naming and memorials policy, approved the 2018-2019 calendar, and heard a budget update before going into executive session.

public_comment.topic: A community group announced a March 8 talk on substance use and families, and asked for a letter of support.
PTO scholarship applications are at the guidance office; the deadline was given as April 12th.

votes.motion: Approve the regular session minutes of January 17
Accept the executive session minutes from several 2017 dates
Not open any school choice slots in grade nine for 2018-19
Allow school choice for students currently in grades nine through eleven so they can stay in grades 10-12
Increase the preschool daily rate by four percent
Increase the preschool daily rate four percent over the next three years (2019, 2020, 2021)
Accept the 2018-2019 school calendar as revised
Go into executive session to discuss strategy for negotiations with the Lunenburg Education Association and non-union contract negotiations

budget_items.what_was_said: Fundraising and donations put money toward a cart, including a matching-grant donation.
Revenue with and without the added teacher was compared, and the entry-level teacher cost was given.
Salaries for teachers and paraprofessionals were said not to include benefits, and tuition covers only a small share.
A four percent increase to the daily rate was moved.
The superintendent called the Chapter 70 allocation disappointing and said a 5.5 percent increase looked limited.

decisions.decision: Extended day sign-ups from both schools will be combined at the primary school.
Reading of the naming and memorials policy was waived; it returns for another reading at the next meeting and will be posted for feedback.

what_happened.line: The committee voted not to open school choice slots in grade nine for 2018-19, and voted to let current students stay under choice through grades 10-12.
The committee voted on a four percent preschool daily rate increase and then on a version spread over the next three years, 2019 through 2021.
The chair announced that the superintendent will retire at the end of the school year.
The committee accepted the revised 2018-2019 school calendar.
The superintendent called the Chapter 70 allocation disappointing in a FY19 budget update, saying the increase looked limited.

why_it_matters: Preschool families face tuition increases set several years ahead, and the debate over an added teacher and classroom space bears on how much of the program is paid by tuition and how much by the school budget, mostly taxes.

A limited state Chapter 70 increase puts more pressure on the FY19 school budget that residents will be asked to vote on at Town Meeting, and the superintendent's retirement means a leadership change during that budget.
